title: From Associations to Activations: Comparing Behavioral and Hidden-State Semantic Geometry in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2602.00628v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: We investigate the extent to which an LLM's hidden-state geometry can be recovered from its behavior in psycholinguistic experiments. Across eight instruction-tuned transformer models, we run two experimental paradigms -- similarity-based forced choice and free association -- over a shared 5,000-word vocabulary, collecting 17.5M+ trials to build behavior-based similarity matrices. Using representational similarity analysis, we compare behavioral geometries to layerwise hidden-state similarity and benchmark against FastText, BERT, and cross-model consensus. We find that forced-choice behavior aligns substantially more with hidden-state geometry than free association. In a held-out-words regression, behavioral similarity (especially forced choice) predicts unseen hidden-state similarities beyond lexical baselines and cross-model consensus, indicating that behavior-only measurements retain recoverable information about internal se

translated_title: 从联结到激活：比较大型语言模型的行为语义几何与隐藏状态语义几何
translated_abstract: 我们研究了在多大程度上能够从大型语言模型在心理语言学实验中的行为表现中恢复其隐藏状态几何结构。我们在八个指令微调的Transformer模型上，针对共享的5000词词表开展了两种实验范式——基于相似性的强制选择和自由联想——收集了超过1750万次试验，以构建基于行为的相似性矩阵。利用表征相似性分析（RSA），我们将行为几何与逐层隐藏状态相似性进行比较，并以FastText、BERT以及跨模型共识作为基准。我们发现，强制选择行为与隐藏状态几何的一致性显著高于自由联想。在留出词回归实验中，行为相似性（尤其是强制选择）能够超越词汇基线和跨模型共识，预测未见过的隐藏状态相似性，这表明仅基于行为的测量仍然保留了可恢复的模型内部语义表征信息。
tldr: 该研究通过大规模心理语言学实验发现，仅从模型行为（尤其是强制选择相似性判断）收集的数据就能预测并恢复大型语言模型隐藏状态中的语义几何结构，证明纯行为测量蕴含着可恢复的内部表征信息。
